title: System Evaluation Report
project: Big Data-Based E-Commerce Demand Forecasting & Inventory Optimization

module_1_ingestion.name: Data Collection & Ingestion
module_1_ingestion.description: Downloaded UCI Online Retail II dataset, converted from Excel to CSV, enriched with simulated fields (Product_Category, Discount, Inventory_Level, Supplier, Delivery_Date).

module_3_preprocessing.name: Data Preprocessing
module_3_preprocessing.description: PySpark pipeline: schema definition, missing value handling, deduplication, outlier removal, date feature extraction, data quality validation.

module_4_analytics.name: Exploratory Big Data Analytics
analytics_produced: KPI calculation (Revenue, AOV, Turnover, Stockout Rate)

assumptions: Inventory levels are SIMULATED (not from a real warehouse system)
Lead time is a configurable constant (real lead times vary by supplier)
Demand is assumed to follow a normal distribution for safety stock calculation
Service level Z-score assumes normally distributed demand during lead time

Hadoop / HDFS.concept: Distributed file storage for large-scale data
Hadoop / HDFS.implementation: HDFS operations module (Module 2). In local mode, mirrors HDFS directory structure. Data organized as raw → processed → results.
Hadoop / HDFS.value: Demonstrates how Big Data is stored across a distributed cluster.

MapReduce.implementation: Spark's internal execution engine uses DAG-based computation that generalizes MapReduce. GroupBy + Agg operations in PySpark are the modern equivalent of MapReduce patterns.
MapReduce.value: Spark provides a more efficient superset of MapReduce.

Apache Spark.implementation: Main processing engine for Modules 3-6. All data cleaning, analytics, feature engineering, and ML use PySpark.
Apache Spark.value: 10-100× faster than MapReduce for iterative workloads like ML.

PySpark.implementation: Used throughout the project for DataFrame operations, Spark SQL queries, and MLlib model training.
PySpark.value: Enables Python developers to leverage Spark's distributed computing.

Spark SQL.implementation: Data quality validation (Module 3), seasonal analysis (Module 4), KPI calculation (Module 4). Uses registerTempView + spark.sql().
Spark SQL.value: Familiar SQL syntax for complex analytical queries on Big Data.

Hive.concept: Data warehouse on Hadoop, SQL-based analytics
Hive.implementation: Spark SQL provides Hive-compatible SQL analytics. The project uses Spark's built-in Hive support through createOrReplaceTempView and SQL queries.
Hive.value: Spark SQL is the modern equivalent of Hive for ad-hoc SQL analytics.

MongoDB.implementation: Module 2: Optional storage for results, forecasts, and inventory recommendations. Schema-flexible document storage.
MongoDB.value: Demonstrates NoSQL storage for semi-structured analytics results.

Machine Learning.implementation: Module 5: Four models trained using Spark MLlib — Moving Average, Linear Regression, Random Forest, GBT.
Machine Learning.value: Distributed ML training on Big Data using Spark's native ML library.

Visualization / BI.implementation: Module 7: Streamlit dashboard with Plotly charts. Executive, Sales, Forecast, and Inventory pages.
Visualization / BI.value: Translates Big Data analytics into actionable business insights.

technology_justification.Why Spark over pandas: Spark processes data in a distributed manner across multiple cores/nodes. For the ~1M record UCI dataset, this demonstrates scalability. In production with billions of records, Spark would be essential while pandas would fail.
technology_justification.Why Spark MLlib over scikit-learn: Spark MLlib trains models on distributed DataFrames without collecting data to a single machine. For large datasets, this avoids memory limits. The project uses MLlib's RandomForestRegressor and GBTRegressor.
technology_justification.Why Parquet over CSV: Parquet is a columnar storage format with built-in compression and schema. It's 2-10× faster for analytical queries and uses 75% less disk space.
technology_justification.Why MongoDB (optional): MongoDB stores semi-structured analytics results (KPIs, forecasts, recommendations) that don't fit a fixed relational schema. Demonstrates NoSQL concepts from the BIS701 syllabus.
technology_justification.Why Streamlit over Power BI: Streamlit integrates directly with the Python analytics pipeline. No separate license required. Results are displayed in real-time from the same data files produced by Spark.
